plan_a_advantages: More varied workout types (hills, tempo, long runs) cater to different aspects of trail running.
Includes active recovery days, crucial for preventing burnout and promoting adaptation.
The inclusion of dedicated hill repeats directly addresses a key component of trail running speed and efficiency.
plan_b_advantages: Tempo runs are more directly focused on improving speed and lactate threshold.
Longer runs are consistently scheduled, which is beneficial for building overall endurance.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, particularly if they are currently at a moderate level. It incorporates a more balanced approach, prioritizing both aerobic endurance and hill strength development with dedicated hill repeats and longer, easier runs. Plan B, while including tempo runs, focuses heavily on threshold training, which could lead to overtraining and hinder overall speed gains if not carefully managed. Plan A’s inclusion of active recovery and varied run types (base endurance, recovery, tempo) provides a more holistic and sustainable path to improvement.
